Keeping in the spirit of ELI5:

Voat has a subscription to something called CloudFare security, what this does is basically put a security guard at the door to Voat, and before anyone can enter the door, the guard checks to make sure it's a real person and not a zombie/robot.
How many times does the security guard have to check our ID before he recognizes us and let's us right in?

Has to check it every time, because others could easily make themselves look like you.

Also the guard is currently on "high alert" because there are a lot of people trying to get in and do bad things, which is why checks are taking a bit longer. If/when it goes back to "low alert" the checks will be faster, you might not even see them.
Too make sure you aren't a bot
As others have said, it's to prevent DDoS attacks and I'm pretty sure it's only temporary.
Is it possible for an average user to mimic bot-like behavior, and subsequently be kicked off?

For the average user I would say no. There are several different type of DDOS attack methods, the simplest being just trying to overwhelm a site with too many simultaneous connections. For more advanced attacks, there are generally certain signatures or packet patterns that can be detected by an IDS/IPS to determine if it is a DDOS, just as your antivirus software looks at known signatures to determine if a file contains a virus.
I would imagine the most common way it could happen is if you're already part of a botnet and you don't know it.
Most likely, no. That's not going to happen unless you're really super good at pressing F5 hundreds of times per second.
